key_insight: An implicit 3D representation of a static environment can be used as a stable scene backbone to generate high-quality cinematic videos with dynamic subjects and user-specified camera trajectories, keeping scene consistency while enabling flexible camera motion.
problem_solved: Reduces the cost and complexity of live-action cinematic production by enabling controllable video synthesis from a few images of a static scene, decoupling scene context from subject motion and camera movement.
method: Build an implicit 3D representation of the static environment from multiple input images (scene backbone).
Decouple the scene from dynamic subject generation and condition subject appearance/motion on a user-specified camera trajectory.
Render view-consistent, photorealistic frames that preserve scene geometry and appearance while animating the subject and camera.
impact: Enables controllable, cost-effective virtual production and content creation workflows by allowing practitioners to synthesize cinematic sequences grounded in real environments, useful for film previsualization, VFX, and dataset generation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multi-view input images → implicit 3D scene model → subject insertion + camera trajectory → rendered video frames.
Frame sequence comparing static scene consistency with moving subject and overlaid camera path.
Side-by-side metric chart (e.g., scene consistency, realism, trajectory adherence) vs. baselines.
3D iconography: camera path curve through a volumetric scene (to convey implicit 3D + trajectory control).
paper_title: CineScene: Implicit 3D as Effective Scene Representation for Cinematic Video Generation
paper_authors: Kaiyi Huang, Yukun Huang, Yu Li, Jianhong Bai, Xintao Wang
